items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: I struck all, struck luck there with fellas like Al Wynn, Tiny Palm... I made good money with Tiny Palm... Tiny Palm was writing all the music and taking everything else.

ctx.x: What happened when you got up to Chicago, Prince?

Well, I went in there with a big show from traveling on the road in the year of 1927. And the show was named the Miramak Miramakers. And after I got in Chicago, well, I struck all, struck luck there with fellas like Al Wynn, Tiny Palm, and Hughie Swift and all them kind of fellas. And I just got good there and made good. So I just stuck on, got to blowing around there. Got up together with a little fella called Francois Louisanans. He had been trying to get a band up together. So we worked together, say about…
Well, to get back to the, you're getting there, you were playing with Miramaks, Miramakas? Miramakas. Now who was the Bronze Bannikens? That was the same album?

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: I made records with Tiny Palm

ctx.x: He was on, he might have played bass on some of them records I made, I don't know, because I was with him right now. But I'll tell you the band, I made records with me and Al Wynn, then I made records with Francois Luzan, I made records with Jimmy Weed, I made records with Tiny Palm, then I made some of my own, you know, with a bunch I had. Somebody else I made records with, I can't think, no. I made records with a lot of guys.
I was just thinking about Tiny Palm, did you ever play any of his arrangements?
